coverage_rules: Every check_*.py validator in tools/ must appear in lint_order exactly once.
Every non-check utility tool in tools/ must appear in utility_tools exactly once.
No validator should be utility-only and no utility should be hidden inside lint_order.
Generated artifacts must name their generator and an available validation path where applicable.
run_lint_suite.py must remain the orchestrator that reads this registry rather than growing a hardcoded validator list.

Toolchain registry coverage, post-readout recheck due-date firebreak validation, owner-packet workbench landing, startup slimming, and release-control refreshes do not close FT-0181 or prove service effectiveness.

Every returned FT-0181 eight-row owner reply CSV should be run through tools/triage_owner_reply_csv.py before any surviving rows move into the owner packet workbench; the tool classification is intake triage, not evidence.
Every returned owner reply CSV should be fingerprinted with tools/receipt_owner_reply_csv.py before staging; the receipt is local metadata only and must not copy raw owner answers or close FT-0181.

Owner-reply workbench seed utilities must be covered by lint and utility registries; seeds are local scratch handoffs only and cannot become SRC2+ acceptance, custody evidence, closure evidence, or public claim support.
lint_lanes must keep owner-reply-field, fast-changed, release-controls, and full-release lanes available so operators can validate changed work without running a monolithic release gate every time.

FT-0181 first-contact packet prep must stay in utility_tools and its validator must stay in lint_order; prepared packets and field-texture memos are PREPARED_NOT_SENT local aids, not evidence, and do not close FT-0181.

FT-0181 runnable field next-action routing must stay utility-only with a validator in owner-reply-field and fast-changed lanes; it may recommend packet, contact, intake, seed, or no-owner-packet commands, but it is not evidence and does not close FT-0181.

FT-0181 local output guards should be shared through tools/ft0181_field_guards.py so packet, route-block, send-log, reask-log, contact, and field-next utilities do not drift on archive-controlled output boundaries.

Rev0271 owner-send-log routing is a local execution firebreak only: prepared packets must route through tools/record_ft0181_owner_send_log.py before any SENT contact-clock status can be recorded; neither the send log nor the contact status closes FT-0181 or proves service effectiveness.

Rev0275 first-packet-decision routing is a local execution gate only: NOT_ACCEPTED workbench seeds must route through tools/record_ft0181_workbench_review.py before any first-packet decision board or re-ask-from-workbench path; neither the review nor its summary is SRC2+ acceptance, custody evidence, closure evidence, or public-claim support.

FT-0181 first-packet decision-board tooling is local/scratch only; a valid board record may source a post-decision change ticket but is not evidence, custody, acceptance, closure, live-window approval, or public-summary support.

FT-0181 live-window card tooling is local/scratch only; a valid post-decision change ticket must route through tools/record_ft0181_live_window_card.py before any readout gate, service-record edit, lifecycle move, custody, acceptance, public-summary change, or closure step.
Owner-route-block tools must be covered so no-send route failures remain executable without creating fake send logs or new doctrine.

Rev0282 owner-reask-log routing is a local execution firebreak only: expired SENT clocks, RE-ASK-ONCE intake bundles, and REASK-OWNER workbench reviews must route through tools/record_ft0181_owner_reask_log.py before any REASK contact-clock status can be recorded; neither the reask log nor the reask contact status closes FT-0181 or proves service effectiveness.

FT-0181 terminal live-window readout tooling is local/scratch only; terminal live-window cards must route through tools/record_ft0181_live_window_readout.py before any post-readout recheck due-date firebreak, service-record edit, lifecycle move, custody, acceptance, public-summary change, or closure step.

Post-readout action dispatch scratch artifacts may convert a terminal readout into one bounded owner-held action/recheck lane without becoming schema evidence, service-record edits, public-language support, lifecycle movement, custody, acceptance, or FT-0181 closure.
FT-0181 post-readout recheck tools must be registered in lint_lanes and utility_tools so due/recheck dates cannot silently expire into closure.

FT-0181 live-window terminal-state brief tooling may compress nonterminal staged/active card handoff to terminal card command skeletons only; it must not record terminal cards, readouts, service-record changes, public claims, custody, acceptance, lifecycle moves, or closure.

Live-window readout brief tooling may compress terminal-readout-to-post-readout-action handoff only; it does not record readouts, dispatch post-readout actions, mutate service records, support public claims, create custody/acceptance, move lifecycle state, or close FT-0181.

lint_lanes.description: FT-0181 first-contact through returned-reply work and post-readout recheck checks only: packet, route-block, send/reask logs, contact status, owner-reply triage/intake/returned-work, workbench review-brief/seed/review, first-packet decision-brief/decision, post-decision ticketing, activation/live-window entry brief, activation, live-window card, terminal/readout-brief/readout, post-readout action-brief/dispatch, due-date recheck brief, and due-date recheck.

Fast lane for changed navigation, registries, owner-request/route-block/send-log/reask-log/contact plumbing, returned-reply work, workbench review-brief/seed/review, first-packet decision-brief/decision, activation-receipt, post-decision change-ticket, live-window card/readout-brief/readout, post-readout action-brief/dispatch, recheck brief/recheck due-date firebreak, watchlists, and generated maps.
Release-control schemas and examples that tend to dominate slow iteration but must pass before packaging.
All lint_order validators in registry order; final handoff gate.
